citationPolicy: Citation IDs identify sources verified at the listed publisher, author, university, standards body, or manufacturer URL. A URL is not a redistribution license. No source documents are vendored here.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Power Electronics, Third Edition
sources.author: Robert W. Erickson; Dragan Maksimović
recommendedSections: Principles of Steady-State Converter Analysis, pp. 15–41
Circuit Averaging, Averaged Switch Modeling, and Simulation, pp. 547–583
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Publisher preview and paid/institutional full-text access; bibliographic metadata is public. Do not redistribute the book PDF.
sources.summary: Rigorous design-oriented treatment of steady state, averaging, converter transfer functions, feedback, DCM, and current-programmed control.
sources.modelingRelevance: Primary derivation reference for averaged plants, operating-mode boundaries, loop construction, and the abstraction ladder.
sources.knownLimitations: COT and multiphase scheduling are not its central focus; supplement with architecture-specific sources.

sources.title: Lecture 5: Intro to DC/DC, Part 1
sources.author: David J. Perreault
recommendedSections: Entire lecture: periodic steady state, volt-second balance, and buck introduction
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: MIT OpenCourseWare; follow the Creative Commons license displayed by the course before redistribution.
sources.summary: Introduces DC/DC conversion and periodic steady-state analysis using buck and boost examples.
sources.modelingRelevance: Establishes switch-state reasoning and state-variable sign conventions before coding or netlisting.
sources.knownLimitations: Lecture scope is foundational and does not cover detailed control.

sources.title: Lecture 7: DC/DC, Part 3
sources.author: David J. Perreault
recommendedSections: Entire lecture: ratings, ripple modeling, and component selection
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: MIT OpenCourseWare; follow the course license before redistribution.
sources.summary: Connects switch waveforms and ripple to component stress and selection.
sources.modelingRelevance: Supplies analytical fixtures for ripple and rating tests.
sources.knownLimitations: Idealized examples require nonideal extensions for production-like models.

sources.title: Lecture 8: DC/DC, Part 4
sources.author: David J. Perreault
recommendedSections: Entire lecture: ripple ratio and discontinuous conduction mode
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: MIT OpenCourseWare; follow the course license before redistribution.
sources.summary: Develops DCM behavior from waveform and ripple reasoning.
sources.modelingRelevance: Guides zero-current event handling and CCM/DCM boundary validation.
sources.knownLimitations: Does not prescribe a particular numerical event solver.

sources.title: Lecture 27: Current-Mode Control
sources.author: David J. Perreault
recommendedSections: Entire lecture: peak current-mode control, averaged model, and ripple instability
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: MIT OpenCourseWare; follow the course license before redistribution.
sources.summary: Introduces current-mode control, linearized modeling, and mitigation of sampled ripple instability.
sources.modelingRelevance: Supports the peak-current pulse simulator and the sampled-data caveats.
sources.knownLimitations: A lecture cannot replace architecture-specific controller documentation.

sources.title: Understanding Buck Power Stages in Switchmode Power Supplies
sources.author: Everett Rogers
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report; link rather than redistribute unless license permits.
sources.summary: Detailed steady-state and small-signal treatment of the buck power stage in CCM and DCM.
sources.modelingRelevance: Provides equations for regression tests and plant transfer-function exercises.
sources.knownLimitations: Explicitly excludes the control circuit and reflects idealized application-report assumptions.

sources.title: Basic Calculation of a Buck Converter's Power Stage
sources.author: Brigitte Hauke
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report.
sources.summary: Practical component-sizing equations with stated application inputs.
sources.modelingRelevance: Useful for operating-point design puzzles and sanity bounds.
sources.knownLimitations: Design shortcuts are not a substitute for dynamic or sampled-data analysis.

sources.title: Loop Stability Analysis of Voltage Mode Buck Regulator With Different Output Capacitor Types – Continuous and Discontinuous Modes
sources.author: Daniel Meeks
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report.
sources.summary: Builds complete loop-gain equations for voltage-mode buck converters with capacitor nonidealities.
sources.modelingRelevance: Prevents omission of modulator and feedback gains in the loop explorer.
sources.knownLimitations: Voltage-mode focus; device and capacitor examples are vendor-contextual.

sources.title: Understanding and Applying Current-Mode Control Theory
sources.author: Robert Sheehan
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report.
sources.summary: Practical current-mode theory including modulator gain, sampling effects, and slope compensation.
sources.modelingRelevance: Basis for current comparator, ramp, blanking, and simplified sampled-data exercises.
sources.knownLimitations: Simplifications are operating-condition dependent; commercial implementations add undocumented details.

sources.title: Power Stage Gain and Slope Compensation Measurement in PCM (Peak Current Mode) BUCK Converter
sources.author: Daniel Jing; Liang Zhang; Zhao Ma
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report.
sources.summary: Shows why power-stage gain and artificial ramp matter and how they may be measured.
sources.modelingRelevance: Connects behavioral parameters to measurable quantities.
sources.knownLimitations: Measurement method and symbols are implementation-specific.

sources.title: Adaptive Constant On-Time (D-CAP™) Control Study in Notebook Applications
sources.author: Chuan Ni; Tateishi Tetsuo
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report; D-CAP is a TI trademark and architecture family.
sources.summary: Compares several buck-control timing methods and explains a representative adaptive on-time implementation and jitter mechanism.
sources.modelingRelevance: Supports the COT taxonomy, timing law, and jitter exercises.
sources.knownLimitations: Vendor-specific D-CAP behavior must not be generalized to every COT controller.

sources.title: D-CAP™ Mode With All-Ceramic Output Capacitor Application
sources.author: Nancy Zhang; Wenkai Wu; Weidong Zhu
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report; architecture-specific.
sources.summary: Implements an external ripple network to support low-ESR ceramic output capacitors in D-CAP mode.
sources.modelingRelevance: Provides a concrete ripple-source and phase-path example for the injection challenge.
sources.knownLimitations: The reported criteria apply to the studied topology and assumptions, not all COT loops.

sources.title: AN-1481 Controlling Output Ripple and Achieving ESR Independence in Constant On-Time (COT) Regulator Designs
sources.author: National Semiconductor / Texas Instruments
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application note.
sources.summary: Examines output-ripple formation and an ESR-independent COT ripple approach.
sources.modelingRelevance: Supports separation of natural capacitor ripple from synthetic feedback ripple.
sources.knownLimitations: Claims about stability and simplicity are tied to the disclosed regulator architecture.

sources.title: Stability Analysis and Design of COT Type-3 Ripple Circuit
sources.author: Texas Instruments
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report.
sources.summary: Analyzes a COT ripple-injection network and practical startup/short-circuit tradeoffs.
sources.modelingRelevance: Demonstrates that ripple networks contribute dynamics and can create non-obvious transient behavior.
sources.knownLimitations: The term Type-3 ripple circuit is not interchangeable with a Type III error-amplifier compensator.

sources.title: D-CAP2™ Frequency Response Model Based on Frequency Domain Analysis of Fixed On-Time With Bottom Detection Having Ripple Injection
sources.author: Toshiyuki (Rick) Zaitsu; Katsuya Goto; Takahiro Miyazaki; Junichi Yamamoto
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report; D-CAP2-specific.
sources.summary: Builds a frequency-domain model including plant, divider, injected-ripple comparator dynamics, and fixed-on-time delay.
sources.modelingRelevance: A strong example of why COT can have a meaningful loop response and compensation-like dynamics.
sources.knownLimitations: Assumes small injected ripple and averaged analysis below switching frequency; architecture-specific.

sources.title: Stability Analysis and Design of D-CAP2 and D-CAP3 Converter – Part 1: How to Select Output Capacitor
sources.author: Andrew Xiong; Zhao Ma
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report; D-CAP2/D-CAP3-specific.
sources.summary: Connects output-capacitor selection and the internal ripple-injection zero to a frequency-loop model.
sources.modelingRelevance: Useful for capacitor/ripple sweeps and architecture-aware stability warnings.
sources.knownLimitations: Do not export its selection boundaries to unrelated COT architectures.

sources.title: Multiphase Buck Design From Start to Finish (Part 1)
sources.author: Carmen Parisi
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application report.
sources.summary: Practical introduction to parallel power phases, 360°/N spacing, and multiphase component design.
sources.modelingRelevance: Defines the baseline symmetric-phase model and ripple-cancellation expectations.
sources.knownLimitations: Controller-specific later design details should not be treated as universal scheduler behavior.

sources.title: Optimal Design for an Interleaved Synchronous Buck Converter Under High-Slew-Rate, Load-Current Transient Conditions
sources.author: Rais Miftakhutdinov
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer technical article.
sources.summary: Relates interleaving and passive design to large, fast load transients.
sources.modelingRelevance: Supports charge-deficit and per-phase slew-limit exercises.
sources.knownLimitations: Optimizations depend on the stated transient and processor-load assumptions.

sources.title: How to Balance Current Using Multiphase Converters
sources.author: George Lakkas
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer technical article.
sources.summary: Explains why current balance is required in both steady state and load transients.
sources.modelingRelevance: Informs mismatch knobs and current-balance error metrics.
sources.knownLimitations: High-level treatment; loop-bandwidth design needs deeper sources.

sources.title: Measurement of Loop Gain in Feedback Systems
sources.author: R. D. Middlebrook
sources.organization: International Journal of Electronics / Taylor & Francis
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Publisher abstract is public; full text may require access. Do not redistribute without permission.
sources.summary: Foundational treatment of measuring loop gain without simply opening a high-gain feedback loop.
sources.modelingRelevance: Grounds loop-injection topology and measurement-validity checks.
sources.knownLimitations: Linear feedback framework; switching and sampled-data limits must be considered separately.

sources.title: Simplified Analysis of PWM Converters Using Model of PWM Switch. Part I: Continuous Conduction Mode
sources.author: Vatché Vorpérian
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: IEEE bibliographic/abstract access; full text may require subscription.
sources.summary: Circuit-oriented averaged PWM-switch model for CCM converters.
sources.modelingRelevance: Supports reusable averaged-switch subcircuits and plant derivation.
sources.knownLimitations: Averaged CCM model does not reproduce individual switching events.

sources.title: Simplified Analysis of PWM Converters Using Model of PWM Switch. Part II: Discontinuous Conduction Mode
sources.author: Vatché Vorpérian
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: IEEE bibliographic/abstract access; full text may require subscription.
sources.summary: Extends the PWM-switch approach to DCM and its additional timing interval.
sources.modelingRelevance: Clarifies why a CCM averaged model cannot be silently reused in DCM.
sources.knownLimitations: Does not produce comparator-level COT timing behavior.

sources.title: A New, Continuous-Time Model for Current-Mode Control
sources.author: Raymond B. Ridley
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: IEEE bibliographic/abstract access; author materials may have separate terms.
sources.summary: Continuous-time approximation that retains key sampled-data behavior to half switching frequency under stated conditions.
sources.modelingRelevance: Prevents the false claim that current-mode control simply removes the inductor at all frequencies.
sources.knownLimitations: Model assumptions and frequency range must be honored; not a universal commercial-controller model.

sources.title: A New Continuous-Time Model for Current-Mode Control With Constant Frequency, Constant On-Time, and Constant Off-Time, in CCM and DCM
sources.author: Raymond B. Ridley
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: IEEE abstract/bibliographic access; full text may require subscription.
sources.summary: Shows that timing law and current programming can coexist, undermining a simplistic COT-versus-current-mode dichotomy.
sources.modelingRelevance: Direct support for the control taxonomy and hybrid architecture lesson.
sources.knownLimitations: Historical model; apply only within its stated assumptions and compare with newer sampled-data work.

sources.title: A Unified Model for Current-Programmed Converters
sources.author: F. Dong Tan; R. D. Middlebrook
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: CaltechAUTHORS record; use the repository's stated rights for any download.
sources.summary: Unified circuit model for current-programmed converters across major topologies.
sources.modelingRelevance: Reference for outer-loop plants and current-programmed limitations.
sources.knownLimitations: Dense derivation; implement only after validating sign and normalization conventions.

sources.title: Topics in the Analysis, Measurement, and Design of High-Performance Switching Regulators
sources.author: Arthur Raymond Brown
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: CaltechTHESIS repository; follow repository rights statement.
sources.summary: Compares state-space averaging and discrete modeling, then studies loop measurements and sensitivity near half switching frequency.
sources.modelingRelevance: Key warning against extending averaged models and conventional Bode interpretation too close to switching frequency.
sources.knownLimitations: Advanced and historically framed; translate notation carefully.

sources.title: A Tutorial and Review Discussion of Modulation, Control and Tuning of High-Performance DC–DC Converters Based on Small-Signal and Large-Signal Approaches
sources.author: Santanu Kapat; Philip T. Krein
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Open-access IEEE publication under CC BY 4.0.
sources.summary: Broad review distinguishing modulation, control, and tuning while connecting small- and large-signal approaches.
sources.modelingRelevance: Primary guardrail against conflating pulse timing with feedback/control structure.
sources.knownLimitations: Breadth requires follow-up in primary architecture sources.

sources.title: Small-Signal Analysis and Design of Constant On-Time Controlled Buck Converters With Duty-Cycle-Independent Quality Factors
sources.author: Wen-Chin Liu; Ching-Hsiang Cheng; Patrick P. Mercier; Chunting Chris Mi
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: IEEE publication; full text may require access. An author-hosted copy exists at San Diego State University subject to its terms.
sources.summary: Derives a COT frequency-domain model and a method for robust quality-factor behavior over duty ratio.
sources.modelingRelevance: Advanced capstone reference for loop dynamics that simple comparator narratives miss.
sources.knownLimitations: Specific modeled COT structure and assumptions; not universal across vendor variants.

sources.title: A Pseudo-Constant Frequency Constant On-Time Buck Converter With Internal Current Ripple Injection and Output DC Offset Cancellation
sources.author: Quan Sun; Yanzhao Ma; Zhengjie Ye; Xiaofei Wang; Hong Zhang
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Open-access IEEE Access paper; this repository stores metadata and a link rather than redistributing the article.
sources.summary: Representative integrated COT architecture using inductor-current ripple injection with low-ESR output capacitors.
sources.modelingRelevance: Provides a non-ESR-ripple architecture for comparison and behavioral abstraction.
sources.knownLimitations: IC implementation details and results do not define generic COT.

sources.title: Constant On-Time Controlled Four-Phase Buck Converter via Two Ways of Saw-Tooth-Wave Circuit and PLL Circuit
sources.author: Yi Xiong; Koyo Asaishi; Natsuko Milli; Yifei Sun; Nobukazu Tsukiji; Yasunori Kobori; Haruo Kobayashi
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: IEEE abstract/bibliographic access; full text may require subscription.
sources.summary: Representative saw-tooth and PLL coordination approaches for a four-phase COT converter.
sources.modelingRelevance: Demonstrates one valid coordinated alternative to free-running phases.
sources.knownLimitations: One disclosed four-phase coordination architecture is not universal and does not establish scheduler fairness for other strategies.

sources.title: A Scalable Multiphase Buck Converter With Average Current Share Bus
sources.author: Wenkang Huang; George Schuellein; Danny Clavette
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer-hosted conference paper; follow site terms for redistribution.
sources.summary: Presents a scalable 1–16 phase architecture using an average current-share bus.
sources.modelingRelevance: Concrete reference for a slower balance loop acting around per-phase controls.
sources.knownLimitations: Implementation-specific and from an earlier VRM generation.

sources.title: FAN23SV10M: 10 A Synchronous Buck Regulator
sources.author: onsemi
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer datasheet; do not infer undisclosed internal circuitry.
sources.summary: Real device example in which fixed on-time ends the high-side pulse while another event requests it.
sources.modelingRelevance: Useful to map minimum timing, protection, and light-load behavior into explicit behavioral parameters.
sources.knownLimitations: Product-specific; its behavior cannot define all COT control.

sources.title: AN-1144: Measuring Output Ripple and Switching Transients in Switching Regulators
sources.author: Aldrick Limjoco
sources.publicationDate: date not shown on current official page
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application note.
sources.summary: Separates coherent output ripple from high-frequency switching transients and shows probe-induced artifacts.
sources.modelingRelevance: Reinforces the distinction between physical ripple, measurement artifact, and numerical artifact.
sources.knownLimitations: Measurement-focused rather than a control-model derivation.

sources.title: PSpice A/D User Guide
sources.author: Cadence Design Systems
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Official Cadence manual for reference; do not redistribute bundled copyrighted documentation.
sources.summary: Authoritative syntax and workflow reference for ABM parts, analyses, expressions, delays, and simulator options.
sources.modelingRelevance: Primary authority for whether a behavioral construct is intended to be PSpice syntax.
sources.knownLimitations: Hosted edition may not match the user's installed release; syntax must still be executed in the target version.

sources.title: DC-DC Converter Design Application Note
sources.author: Cadence Design Systems
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Official Cadence application note; use linked design files under their supplied terms.
sources.summary: Cadence example workflow for simulating and analyzing a switching power converter.
sources.modelingRelevance: Anchors tool-specific analysis and plot workflow.
sources.knownLimitations: Not a COT or multiphase reference and does not validate this project's netlists.

sources.title: PSpice: Single Switch Forward Converter
sources.author: Cadence Design Systems
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Official Cadence application note.
sources.summary: Worked switched-converter example using PSpice A/D and ABM methods.
sources.modelingRelevance: Shows hierarchical behavioral decomposition even though the topology is not a buck.
sources.knownLimitations: Forward-converter details must not be copied into buck physics.

sources.title: Creating Custom Plot Window With PSpice
sources.author: Cadence Design Systems
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Official Cadence application note.
sources.summary: Shows ABM-based computed traces and custom plot-window construction.
sources.modelingRelevance: Supports documented measurements for phase spacing, frequency, and current mismatch.
sources.knownLimitations: Plotting guidance is not evidence that a model is physically valid.

sources.title: PSpice
sources.author: Cadence Design Systems
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public product page; features and licensing can change by release/edition.
sources.summary: Current official overview of PSpice capabilities and editions.
sources.modelingRelevance: Scopes available analysis families but is not a syntax reference.
sources.knownLimitations: Marketing overview; verify precise capability in the installed license and user guide.

sources.title: PSpice for TI Design and Simulation Tool
sources.author: Texas Instruments; Cadence Design Systems
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Official tool/download page; license restrictions apply.
sources.summary: Describes the Cadence-powered PSpice for TI edition and its offline capability.
sources.modelingRelevance: Potential execution environment for later manual validation, subject to edition limits.
sources.knownLimitations: Availability of generic third-party models and features may differ from full Cadence PSpice.

sources.title: Quick Reference Guide to TI Buck Switching DC/DC Application Notes
sources.author: Alex Da Silva; Yann Ducommun
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer index; use it to discover, then verify, individual reports.
sources.summary: Curated index of TI buck-converter application notes grouped by design task.
sources.modelingRelevance: Research map and gap-checking aid rather than a claim-level source.
sources.knownLimitations: Vendor-only index and not itself proof for technical claims.

sources.title: Buck Power Stage Design Equations
sources.author: Analog Devices
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application note.
sources.summary: Independent manufacturer cross-check for practical buck component equations.
sources.modelingRelevance: Reduces reliance on a single vendor's notation and heuristics.
sources.knownLimitations: Component sizing is not a full dynamic/control model.

sources.title: Dual-Phase Operation in Multiphase Buck Applications
sources.author: Infineon Technologies
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer application note.
sources.summary: Examines driving multiple stages and resulting current relationships in a multiphase application.
sources.modelingRelevance: Useful counterexample to assuming one PWM command implies independent phase regulation.
sources.knownLimitations: Product-family context and dual-phase focus.

sources.title: Achieving Fast Load-Transient Response and Low EMI With the AECM DC/DC Control Topology
sources.author: Vincent Zhang
sources.licenseOrAccessNote: Public manufacturer technical article; architecture-specific.
sources.summary: Introduces TI's fixed-frequency advanced emulated current-mode topology and compares its loop concept with representative PCM and D-CAP2 structures.
sources.modelingRelevance: Concrete evidence that timing method, sensed or emulated current information, and loop architecture form a richer taxonomy than a single control-mode label.
sources.knownLimitations: Vendor-authored introduction to AECM, not a neutral control comparison or a source for generic D-CAP3, minimum-off-time, or phase-shedding claims.
